0.long_answer: The ASPM gene, located on chromosome 1q31, has been identified as a major contributor to autosomal recessive primary microcephaly when mutated. Defects in this gene disrupt normal mitotic spindle function in neural progenitor cells, which is critical for cell division during brain development. As a result, mutation of the ASPM gene leads to a significant reduction in brain size, a hallmark of microcephaly. Studies have shown that alterations in ASPM account for a significant proportion of microcephaly cases, making it one of the primary genetic causes of this neurodevelopmental disorder.
